summary.text: 明 is used for “bright” and “clear.” Early records show more than one form: some join 日 “sun” and 月 “moon,” while another joins 月 with a window-shaped 囧. The early forms are linked to both dawn and brightness, but their original meaning and the order of those senses are unresolved. [ref014, ref016, ref020]

formation.text: The 日+月 construction is best described as semantic: 日 and 月 are meaningful graphic elements associated with celestial light. One reported interpretation reads their pairing as dawn, with the sun rising before the moon has set; another takes them together as brightness. A separate early form, 朙, joins 月 and window-shaped 囧 and was interpreted as moonlight entering through a window; 囧 is also reported as a phonetic element there, though the sound analysis is not independently demonstrated by the evidence available here. These are distinct early analyses, not proof that one was the sole original construction. [ref003, ref010, ref016, ref020, ref021]

components.text: In this early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun and 月 the moon; together they contribute the celestial-light imagery associated with the brightness reading, and with dawn in one interpretation. Both are pictorial elements in this construction. [ref016, ref020]
In this early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon and 日 the sun; their pairing is associated with brightness or, in one interpretation, dawn. 月 is pictorial in this construction. [ref016, ref020]

In the separately attested form 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image. It is also reported to supply a sound cue, but the available comparison does not establish that role: the same-system Old Chinese forms differ, and the window's ancient spoken name is unknown. [ref016, ref017, ref020, ref021]

sound_limitation.text: The reported phonetic role is not independently established by the available sound evidence. Baxter–Sagart gives 明 *mraŋ and 囧 *k-mraŋʔ in the same Old Chinese system, and the original spoken name of the depicted window is not established; these facts do not prove a historical sound correspondence. [ref016, ref017, ref021]

sound.text: A reported Old Chinese comparison is 囧 *k-mraŋʔ beside 明 *mraŋ, both in Baxter–Sagart 1.1. The forms differ in their initial and final; this comparison therefore does not by itself demonstrate the reported phonetic role. [ref012, ref013, ref017]

components.text: In 朙, 月 depicts the moon and contributes the moonlight interpretation. [ref016, ref020, ref021]

history.text: 日+月 forms are reported in oracle-bone and bronze writing; other early forms include 朙, with 月+囧. The sources also report 目+月 and 田+月 forms, but 目+月 is too fragmentary for secure identification in one account, and 田 may reflect corruption of 日 or 囧. 明 is described as an ancient form of the seal graph 朙 in the Shuowen tradition; that historical analysis does not establish that 朙 was the only early form. [ref010, ref014, ref015, ref016, ref020, ref021]

A later Qin manuscript’s 目-form is reported as a likely corruption of 囧, while the early 目+月 examples remain uncertain. These reports concern graphic interpretation, not a settled sequence for all forms. [ref003, ref016, ref020]

uncertainties.text: The dossier reports dawn and brightness uses in oracle-bone material, but does not establish which meaning came first. It also does not independently resolve the phonetic analysis of 囧 in 朙, or establish the original spoken name of the depicted window. [ref016, ref017, ref020, ref021]

The reported early inscription readings and graphic interpretations were not checked against the underlying inscription images in this research pass; exact dates for the cited examples were not established. [ref016, ref020]

senses.text: Brightness is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples. The available evidence does not show whether this preceded or followed the attested dawn use. [ref016, ref020]

Dawn is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples, and a later cited Shijing line also illustrates daybreak. Its chronological relation to the brightness sense is unresolved. [ref015, ref016, ref020]
Clear or manifest uses are reported in bronze inscriptions. The evidence lists this use but does not specify the semantic path from brightness or dawn. [ref016, ref020]
Modern dictionary glosses include bright, light, and clear. [ref004, ref007]

limitations.text: Early brightness and dawn attestations are both reported, but their relative chronology and the development of later clear/manifest uses are not established by this dossier. [ref016, ref020]

overview.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early forms include sun-plus-moon imagery and a separate moon-and-window form; sources associate them with brightness, dawn, or moonlight, without settling one original meaning. [ref016, ref020]

components.text: 日 pictures the sun in the early sun-and-moon construction. [ref016, ref020]
月 pictures the moon in the early sun-and-moon construction. [ref016, ref020]
囧 is described as a lattice window in 朙; its reported sound role remains uncertain. [ref016, ref017, ref021]
月 pictures the moon in 朙, the form interpreted as moonlight through a window. [ref016, ref020, ref021]

relationships.text: In the reported early 日+月 form, 日 depicts the sun as part of the celestial-light scene associated with 明. [ref016, ref020]
In the reported early 日+月 form, 月 depicts the moon as part of the celestial-light scene associated with 明. [ref016, ref020]

The Shuowen account identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙, whose analysis joins 月 and 囧. This is a reported historical graph relation, not proof that 朙 was the only early form. [ref015, ref019, ref021]
In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image. [ref016, ref020, ref021]
In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the reported moonlight-through-a-window interpretation. [ref016, ref020, ref021]

The source reports 囧 as a sound element in 朙. The same-system Baxter–Sagart readings 囧 *k-mraŋʔ and 明 *mraŋ differ; the available evidence does not demonstrate how the phonetic analysis accounts for that difference. [ref016, ref017, ref021]
